title: Ancient Egyptian civilization
summary: Radiocarbon dating puts the foundation of the Egyptian state, with the accession of King Aha, between 3111 and 3045 BCE. The Penn Museum dates the First Dynasty to about 3100 to 2900 BCE. Memphis and its pyramid fields from Giza to Dahshur date from the Old Kingdom, and Thebes, with the Valleys of the Kings and Queens, is a striking testimony to Egyptian civilization at its height.

uncertainty.note: Start is the traditional c. 3100 BCE foundation of Dynasty I (radiocarbon Bayesian models place Aha's accession at 3111–3045 BCE); end is the Roman conquest of Ptolemaic Egypt following the death of Cleopatra VII in 30 BCE.

when.display: c. 3100 BCE – 30 BCE (First Dynasty to Roman conquest)

where.modern_name: Mit Rahina (Memphis), Giza Governorate, Egypt (ancient capital of unified Egypt from the First Dynasty)
where.historical_name: Ineb-hedj / Men-nefer (Memphis), Upper and Lower Egypt (Kemet, Nile Valley)

importance.justification: Ancient Egyptian civilization maintained three millennia of continuous statecraft, monumental architecture, writing, and religion that defined early Mediterranean and African antiquity.

related.because: The political unification of Upper and Lower Egypt under the First Dynasty established the territorial foundation of the civilization.
